title: です
meaning: "is / am / are" — polite copula linking a noun or adjective to the topic.
simpleExplanation: です is the polite word for "is / am / are". You put it at the very end of the sentence after a noun or an adjective: 学生です "(I) am a student", 大きいです "(it) is big". It never changes for I / you / he / they, so one word covers every English form of "to be". Japanese often leaves out the subject when it is obvious, so 学生です on its own can mean "I am a student".
whenUsed: Used whenever you speak politely: to teachers, shop staff, strangers, colleagues, and in almost every N5 exam sentence. It is the safe default form for a beginner. With friends and family, the plain form だ (or nothing) is used instead.
formation: い-adjective + です  (大きいです)

examples.reading: わたしは がくせいです。
examples.note: The most basic Japanese sentence: topic + noun + です.
これ (this) works just like any other noun before です.

examples.reading: とうきょうは おおきいです。
examples.note: After an い-adjective, です only adds politeness; the adjective already means "is big".

examples.ja: 田中さんは会社員です。
examples.reading: たなかさんは かいしゃいんです。
examples.en: Mr Tanaka is a company employee.
examples.note: Same です whether the subject is I, you or Mr Tanaka.

examples.reading: この みせは ゆうめいです。
examples.note: 有名 is a な-adjective; before です it looks just like a noun.

similarGrammar.difference: Plain / casual "is". Same meaning, used with friends and inside longer sentences (と思う, から).
The negative of です: "is not".
The past of です: "was / were".

commonMistakes.why: です is used once, at the end. It is not a verb that needs another verb after it.
です goes after nouns and adjectives, not after a verb. Verbs have their own polite ending ます.

commonMistakes.wrong: 田中さんは学生でいます。
commonMistakes.why: English "is" maps to です for nouns/adjectives; います means "exists" and is used for "there is (a person)".

usageNotes: です makes the sentence polite. It does not change for person or number (I/you/they all use です). After an い-adjective, です only adds politeness — the adjective itself carries tense.
jlptTips: N5 rarely tests です alone. It appears in almost every sentence, so the real question is usually the particle before it (は, の) or the tense (です vs でした).
If the blank is at the end of a sentence after a noun and the options are です / ます / います / あります, choose です. ます needs a verb stem, and います／あります need が before them.
